newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Kok sees European cooperation not federation.
newsitem.headline: Kok sees European cooperation not federation.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Friday the idea of a federal Europe was losing ground and that it was better to aim for cooperation in the region than for a federal structure.

"We should not think, in my view, in terms of a United States of Europe. We should think in terms of what we can do in the total sum of individual states with their own identity where - if we act together - a better performance can be reached," Kok said in an interview with business broadcaster CNBC.

"There has been a time somewhere in the 80s and perhaps even in the beginning of the 90s where the ideal of a federal Europe was broadly shared in a number of continental countries, but that time is behind us now," Kok said.

"I think we talk about the best possible type of cooperation where we transfer certain responsibilities to the European level but only a selected number of issues with well organised political control, not only by member states but also by the European Parliament," Kok said.
